source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: 2 Samuel 1–5: all 135 verses bind one-to-one to the matching Hebrew records.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps the opening’s linked events and exact interval.
verses.before: After the death of Saul, when David had returned from striking the Amalekites, David remained two days in Ziklag.
verses.after: After Saul’s death, David returned from striking the Amalekites and stayed in Ziklag for two days.
verses.tsw_comparator: After the death of Saul, when David had returned from striking the Amalekites, David remained two days in Ziklag.

verses.rationale: Preserves third day, mourning signs and obeisance.
verses.before: On the third day, look, a man came from the camp from Saul, with his clothes torn and dirt upon his head. When he came to David, he fell to the ground and bowed down.
verses.after: On the third day a man arrived from Saul’s camp, his clothes torn and dirt on his head. When he reached David, he fell to the ground and bowed.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the third day, look, a man came from the camp from Saul, with his clothes torn and dirt upon his head. When he came to David, he fell to the ground and bowed down.

verses.rationale: Keeps the speaker’s claimed escape without adding battlefield status.
verses.before: David said to him, “From where have you come?” He said to him, “I have escaped from the camp of Israel.”
verses.after: David asked, “Where have you come from?” He answered, “I escaped from Israel’s camp.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to him, “From where have you come?” He said to him, “I have escaped from the camp of Israel.”

verses.rationale: Preserves widening losses and final personal news.
verses.before: David said to him, “What happened? Please tell me.” He said, “The people fled from the battle, and many of the people also fell and died. Saul and Jonathan his son also died.”
verses.after: “What happened?” David asked. “Please tell me.” He said, “The troops fled from the battle. Many fell and died. Saul and his son Jonathan are dead too.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to him, “What happened? Please tell me.” He said, “The people fled from the battle, and many of the people also fell and died. Saul and Jonathan his son also died.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the request for evidence and both names.
verses.before: David said to the young man who told him, “How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?”
verses.after: David asked the young man bringing the news, “How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to the young man who told him, “How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?”

verses.rationale: Retains the messenger’s claimed chance arrival and spear, distinct from the earlier sword account.
verses.before: The young man who told him said, “By chance I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and look, Saul was leaning on his spear, and look, the chariots and horsemen were closing in on him.
verses.after: The young man answered, “I happened to be on Mount Gilboa. Saul was leaning on his spear, and the chariots and horsemen were closing in on him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The young man who told him said, “By chance I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and look, Saul was leaning on his spear, and look, the chariots and horsemen were closing in on him.

verses.rationale: Preserves call and response inside reported speech.
verses.before: He turned behind him, saw me, and called to me. I said, ‘Here I am.’
verses.after: He turned, saw me, and called. I answered, ‘Here I am.’
verses.tsw_comparator: He turned behind him, saw me, and called to me. I said, ‘Here I am.’

verses.rationale: Follows qere first-person answer and retains ethnic identification.
verses.before: He said to me, ‘Who are you?’ I said to him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’
verses.after: He asked, ‘Who are you?’ I told him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to me, ‘Who are you?’ I said to him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’

verses.rationale: Uses agony for the rare term and preserves reported request and continued life; uncertainty noted.
verses.before: Then he said to me, ‘Please stand over me and put me to death, for agony has seized me, though all my life is still in me.’
verses.after: Then he said, ‘Stand over me and kill me. Agony has gripped me, yet my life is still in me.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to me, ‘Please stand over me and put me to death, for agony has seized me, though all my life is still in me.’

verses.rationale: Preserves killing claim and royal objects without validating or harmonizing the account.
verses.before: So I stood over him and put him to death, because I knew that he could not live after he had fallen. I took the crown that was on his head and the armlet that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord.”
verses.after: So I stood over him and killed him, knowing he would not survive his fall. I took the crown from his head and the armlet from his arm and brought them here to my lord.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So I stood over him and put him to death, because I knew that he could not live after he had fallen. I took the crown that was on his head and the armlet that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord.”

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily mourning and collective participation.
verses.before: Then David took hold of his clothes and tore them, and so did all the men who were with him.
verses.after: David seized his clothes and tore them. All the men with him did the same.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then David took hold of his clothes and tore them, and so did all the men who were with him.

verses.rationale: Retains all four objects of mourning and three actions.
verses.before: They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul, for Jonathan his son, for the people of the LORD, and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
verses.after: They mourned, wept, and fasted until evening for Saul, for his son Jonathan, for the LORD’s people, and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul, for Jonathan his son, for the people of the LORD, and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

verses.rationale: Preserves the fuller social identification in the repeated question.
verses.before: David said to the young man who told him, “Where are you from?” He said, “I am the son of a resident alien, an Amalekite.”
verses.after: David asked the young messenger, “Where are you from?” He answered, “I am the son of an Amalekite resident foreigner.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to the young man who told him, “Where are you from?” He said, “I am the son of a resident alien, an Amalekite.”

verses.rationale: Retains hand/anointed language from David’s refusals to kill Saul.
verses.before: David said to him, “How were you not afraid to stretch out your hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?”
verses.after: David said, “How were you not afraid to raise your hand and destroy the LORD’s anointed?”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to him, “How were you not afraid to stretch out your hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?”

verses.rationale: Keeps David’s order and resulting execution explicit.
verses.before: Then David called one of the young men and said, “Come near; strike him.” So he struck him, and he died.
verses.after: He called one of the young men and said, “Go and strike him down.” The man struck him, and he died.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then David called one of the young men and said, “Come near; strike him.” So he struck him, and he died.

verses.rationale: Preserves responsibility idiom and the stated basis in his own testimony.
verses.before: David said to him, “Your blood is upon your own head, for your own mouth testified against you, saying, ‘I put the LORD’s anointed to death.’”
verses.after: David said to him, “Your blood is on your own head. Your own mouth testified against you when you said, ‘I killed the LORD’s anointed.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to him, “Your blood is upon your own head, for your own mouth testified against you, saying, ‘I put the LORD’s anointed to death.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps named mourned figures and introduces the poem as lament.
verses.before: David lamented with this lament over Saul and over Jonathan his son.
verses.after: David lamented Saul and his son Jonathan with this lament,
verses.tsw_comparator: David lamented with this lament over Saul and over Jonathan his son.

verses.rationale: Treats bow as title contextually, with archery alternative noted; retains named source book.
verses.before: He said to teach the children of Judah “The Bow.” Look, it is written in the Book of Jashar.
verses.after: and ordered that the people of Judah be taught “The Bow.” It is written in the Book of Jashar:
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to teach the children of Judah “The Bow.” Look, it is written in the Book of Jashar.

verses.rationale: Keeps ambiguous splendor/gazelle term as splendor and establishes repeated refrain.
verses.before: Your glory, Israel, lies slain upon your heights. How the mighty have fallen!
verses.after: “Your splendor, Israel, lies slain on your heights. How the mighty have fallen!
verses.tsw_comparator: Your glory, Israel, lies slain upon your heights. How the mighty have fallen!

verses.rationale: Preserves parallel negative commands and the specifically female celebrants.
verses.before: Do not tell it in Gath; do not proclaim it in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
verses.after: Do not tell it in Gath; do not announce it in Ashkelon’s streets, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised celebrate.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not tell it in Gath; do not proclaim it in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.

verses.rationale: Retains difficult offering-fields phrase and shield anointing rather than silently moving the oil to Saul.
verses.before: Mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew or rain upon you, nor fields of offerings, for there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.
verses.after: Mountains of Gilboa, let no dew or rain fall on you, let there be no fields yielding offerings! There the warriors’ shield was defiled, Saul’s shield, no longer anointed with oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew or rain upon you, nor fields of offerings, for there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.

verses.rationale: Preserves blood/fat imagery and both weapon movements.
verses.before: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not turn back, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
verses.after: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of warriors, Jonathan’s bow did not turn back; Saul’s sword did not return empty.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not turn back, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.

verses.rationale: Keeps the lament’s praise as poetry without reconciling their recorded conflicts.
verses.before: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided. They were swifter than eagles; they were stronger than lions.
verses.after: Saul and Jonathan, loved and dear in life, were not parted in death. They were swifter than eagles, stronger than lions.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided. They were swifter than eagles; they were stronger than lions.

verses.rationale: Preserves female addressees and concrete gifts.
verses.before: Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet with luxury, who put ornaments of gold upon your garments.
verses.after: Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and finery, who set ornaments of gold on your garments.
verses.tsw_comparator: Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet with luxury, who put ornaments of gold upon your garments.

verses.rationale: Repeats the refrain and retains the shifting second-person address.
verses.before: How the mighty have fallen among the battle! Jonathan lies slain upon your heights.
verses.after: How the mighty have fallen in the midst of battle! Jonathan lies slain on your heights.
verses.tsw_comparator: How the mighty have fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan lies slain upon your heights.

verses.rationale: Preserves unqualified love and its comparison without assigning a modern category or diminishing intimacy.
verses.before: I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan. You were very pleasant to me. Your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.
verses.after: I grieve for you, my brother Jonathan. You were deeply dear to me. Your love for me was wondrous, beyond the love of women.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan. You were very pleasant to me. Your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.

verses.rationale: Keeps the third refrain and concluding weapons image.
verses.before: How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!
verses.after: How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!”
verses.tsw_comparator: How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!

verses.rationale: Retains two-stage inquiry and named destination.
verses.before: After this David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Will I go up to one of the cities of Judah?” The LORD said to him, “Go up.” David said, “Where will I go up?” He said, “To Hebron.”
verses.after: After this David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go up to one of Judah’s towns?” The LORD said, “Go up.” David asked, “Where?” “To Hebron,” came the answer.
verses.tsw_comparator: After this David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall I go up to one of the cities of Judah?” The LORD said to him, “Go up.” David said, “Where shall I go up?” He said, “To Hebron.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both wives and the retained former-husband identification.
verses.before: So David went up there, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail, the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
verses.after: David went up there with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the wife of Nabal of Carmel.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David went up there, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail, the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

verses.rationale: Keeps family migration and surrounding settlements.
verses.before: David also brought up the men who were with him, each with his household, and they lived in the cities of Hebron.
verses.after: He also brought his men, each with his household, and they settled in the towns around Hebron.
verses.tsw_comparator: David also brought up the men who were with him, each with his household, and they lived in the cities of Hebron.

verses.rationale: Preserves initial limited kingship and the new burial report.
verses.before: Then the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. They told David, saying, “The men of Jabesh-Gilead were the ones who buried Saul.”
verses.after: The men of Judah came and anointed David king over the house of Judah. David was told that the men of Jabesh-gilead had buried Saul.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. They told David, saying, “The men of Jabesh-Gilead were the ones who buried Saul.”

verses.rationale: Keeps burial as loyal kindness and Saul as their lord.
verses.before: So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-Gilead and said to them, “Blessed are you by the LORD because you showed this steadfast love to your lord Saul and buried him.
verses.after: He sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead: “May the LORD bless you for showing this steadfast love to your lord Saul by burying him.
verses.tsw_comparator: So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-Gilead and said to them, “Blessed are you by the LORD because you showed this steadfast love to your lord Saul and buried him.

verses.rationale: Retains paired steadfast love/faithfulness and David’s reciprocal promise.
verses.before: And now may the LORD show steadfast love and faithfulness to you. I also will do good to you because you have done this thing.
verses.after: May the LORD now show you steadfast love and faithfulness. I too will do you good because you have done this.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now may the LORD show steadfast love and faithfulness to you. I also will do good to you because you have done this thing.

verses.rationale: Keeps hand image and the political announcement within the encouragement.
verses.before: And now let your hands be strong and be courageous, for Saul your lord is dead, and the house of Judah has anointed me king over them.”
verses.after: Let your hands be strong, and be brave. Your lord Saul is dead, and the house of Judah has anointed me king over them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now let your hands be strong and be courageous, for Saul your lord is dead, and the house of Judah has anointed me king over them.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Abner’s initiative and surviving Saulide.
verses.before: Yet Abner son of Ner, commander of Saul’s army, took Ish-Bosheth son of Saul and brought him across to Mahanaim.
verses.after: But Abner son of Ner, Saul’s army commander, took Saul’s son Ish-bosheth across to Mahanaim.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Abner son of Ner, commander of Saul’s army, took Ish-Bosheth son of Saul and brought him across to Mahanaim.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned Ashurites and complete territory list; identity uncertainty noted.
verses.before: He made him king over Gilead, the Ashurites, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin, and all Israel.
verses.after: He made him king over Gilead, the Ashurites, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin, and all Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made him king over Gilead, the Ashurites, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin, and all Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps age, duration and exception without harmonizing the next duration.
verses.before: Ish-Bosheth son of Saul was forty years old when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years. Only the house of Judah followed David.
verses.after: Ish-bosheth son of Saul was forty years old when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years. Only the house of Judah followed David.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ish-Bosheth son of Saul was forty years old when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years. Only the house of Judah followed David.

verses.rationale: Preserves the different reign length exactly.
verses.before: The number of days that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
verses.after: David was king over the house of Judah in Hebron for seven years and six months.
verses.tsw_comparator: The number of days that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

verses.rationale: Keeps leaders, allegiance and route.
verses.before: Abner son of Ner and the servants of Ish-Bosheth son of Saul went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
verses.after: Abner son of Ner and the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abner son of Ner and the servants of Ish-Bosheth son of Saul went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

verses.rationale: Preserves maternal identification and confrontational seating.
verses.before: Joab son of Zeruiah and the servants of David went out and met them by the pool of Gibeon. They sat down, these on one side of the pool and those on the other side of the pool.
verses.after: Joab son of Zeruiah and David’s servants also went out. They met at the pool of Gibeon and sat on opposite sides of the pool.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joab son of Zeruiah and the servants of David went out and met them by the pool of Gibeon. They sat down, these on one side of the pool and those on the other side of the pool.

verses.rationale: Keeps play/contest language whose deadly result follows, with note rather than sanitization.
verses.before: Abner said to Joab, “Please let the young men arise and play before us.” Joab said, “Let them arise.”
verses.after: Abner said to Joab, “Let the young men rise and put on a contest before us.” Joab answered, “Let them rise.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Abner said to Joab, “Please let the young men arise and play before us.” Joab said, “Let them arise.”

verses.rationale: Preserves twelve on each side and political identifications.
verses.before: So they arose and crossed over by number: twelve for Benjamin and Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, and twelve from the servants of David.
verses.after: They rose and crossed over in equal numbers: twelve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve from David’s servants.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they arose and crossed over by number: twelve for Benjamin and Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, and twelve from the servants of David.

verses.rationale: Keeps simultaneous mutual killing and uncertain place name.
verses.before: Each seized his opponent by the head and thrust his sword into his opponent’s side, so they fell down together. Therefore that place was called Helkath-Hazzurim, which is at Gibeon.
verses.after: Each grabbed his opponent’s head and drove his sword into his opponent’s side. They fell together. The place at Gibeon was called Helkath-hazzurim.
verses.tsw_comparator: Each seized his opponent by the head and thrust his sword into his opponent’s side, so they fell down together. Therefore that place was called Helkath-Hazzurim, which is at Gibeon.

verses.rationale: Preserves escalation from contest into battle.
verses.before: The battle was very fierce that day, and Abner and the men of Israel were struck before the servants of David.
verses.after: The battle that day was very fierce. Abner and Israel’s men were defeated by David’s servants.
verses.tsw_comparator: The battle was very fierce that day, and Abner and the men of Israel were struck before the servants of David.

verses.rationale: Retains all siblings and animal comparison.
verses.before: The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel was swift on his feet like one of the gazelles that are in the field.
verses.after: Zeruiah’s three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel was as swift-footed as a gazelle in the open country.
verses.tsw_comparator: The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel was swift on his feet like one of the gazelles that are in the field.

verses.rationale: Keeps single-minded pursuit and directional repetition.
verses.before: Asahel pursued Abner and did not turn to the right or to the left from following Abner.
verses.after: Asahel pursued Abner, turning neither right nor left as he followed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Asahel pursued Abner and did not turn to the right or to the left from following Abner.

verses.rationale: Preserves recognition before warnings.
verses.before: Abner turned behind him and said, “Is that you, Asahel?” He said, “It is I.”
verses.after: Abner looked behind him and asked, “Is that you, Asahel?” “It is,” he answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abner turned behind him and said, “Is that you, Asahel?” He said, “It is I.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the offered alternative victim and refusal without making it benevolent in narration.
verses.before: Abner said to him, “Turn aside to your right or to your left, seize one of the young men, and take his spoil for yourself.” But Asahel was not willing to turn aside from following him.
verses.after: Abner said, “Turn to your right or left. Seize one of the young men and take his gear.” But Asahel would not turn away from him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abner said to him, “Turn aside to your right or to your left, seize one of the young men, and take his spoil for yourself.” But Asahel was not willing to turn aside from following him.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated warning and concern about the surviving brother.
verses.before: Abner again said to Asahel, “Turn aside from following me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How then could I lift my face to Joab your brother?”
verses.after: Abner warned him again, “Turn away! Why should I strike you to the ground? How could I face your brother Joab?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Abner again said to Asahel, “Turn aside from following me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How then could I lift my face to Joab your brother?”

verses.rationale: Retains unusual weapon end, bodily wound and halted onlookers.
verses.before: But he refused to turn aside. So Abner struck him in the belly with the butt end of the spear, and the spear came out behind him. He fell there and died on the spot. And everyone who came to the place where Asahel fell and died stood still.
verses.after: Asahel refused to turn away. Abner struck him in the belly with the butt of his spear, and the spear came out through his back. He fell and died there. Everyone who came to the place where Asahel had fallen stood still.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he refused to turn aside. So Abner struck him in the belly with the butt end of the spear, and the spear came out behind him. He fell there and died on the spot. And everyone who came to the place where Asahel fell and died stood still.

verses.rationale: Keeps pursuers, sunset and exact place sequence.
verses.before: Yet Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. The sun was going down when they came to the hill of Ammah, which is before Giah, on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.
verses.after: Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. As the sun set, they reached the hill of Ammah opposite Giah, on the road to the wilderness of Gibeon.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. The sun was going down when they came to the hill of Ammah, which is before Giah, on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.

verses.rationale: Preserves regrouping and defensive position.
verses.before: The children of Benjamin gathered themselves together behind Abner and became one group, and they stood on the top of a hill.
verses.after: The Benjaminites rallied behind Abner, formed a single group, and took their stand on a hilltop.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Benjamin gathered themselves together behind Abner and became one group, and they stood on the top of a hill.

verses.rationale: Keeps sword-devouring image and appeal to kinship.
verses.before: Then Abner called to Joab and said, “Will the sword devour forever? Do you not know that it will be bitter in the end? How long before you tell the people to turn back from pursuing their brothers?”
verses.after: Abner called to Joab, “Must the sword devour forever? Do you not know this will end in bitterness? How long before you tell the men to stop pursuing their brothers?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Abner called to Joab and said, “Shall the sword devour forever? Do you not know that it will be bitter in the end? How long before you tell the people to turn back from pursuing their brothers?”

verses.rationale: Uses until-morning reading of the counterfactual; alternate reference to earlier challenge noted.
verses.before: Joab said, “As God lives, if you had not spoken, then surely only by morning would the people have gone up, each from pursuing his brother.”
verses.after: Joab answered, “As God lives, if you had not spoken, the men would have kept pursuing their brothers until morning.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Joab said, “As God lives, if you had not spoken, then surely only by morning would the people have gone up, each from pursuing his brother.”

verses.rationale: Preserves three cessation clauses and signaling instrument.
verses.before: So Joab blew the ram’s horn, and all the people stopped. They pursued Israel no more, and they fought no more.
verses.after: Joab sounded the ram’s horn. All the troops halted, stopped pursuing Israel, and ceased fighting.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joab blew the ram’s horn, and all the people stopped. They pursued Israel no more, and they fought no more.

verses.rationale: Keeps pinned Bithron rather than replacing it with morning; geography uncertainty noted.
verses.before: Abner and his men walked through the Arabah all that night. They crossed the Jordan, walked through all the Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.
verses.after: Abner and his men walked through the Arabah all that night. They crossed the Jordan, passed through all Bithron, and reached Mahanaim.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abner and his men walked through the Arabah all that night. They crossed the Jordan, walked through all the Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.

verses.rationale: Preserves nineteen plus Asahel, not nineteen including him.
verses.before: Joab returned from pursuing Abner and gathered all the people. From the servants of David, nineteen men were missing, besides Asahel.
verses.after: Joab returned from pursuing Abner and gathered all his men. Nineteen of David’s servants were missing, besides Asahel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joab returned from pursuing Abner and gathered all the people. From the servants of David, nineteen men were missing, besides Asahel.

verses.rationale: Retains opposing death total exactly.
verses.before: But the servants of David had struck down from Benjamin and the men of Abner three hundred sixty men who died.
verses.after: David’s servants had killed three hundred sixty men from Benjamin and Abner’s forces.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the servants of David had struck down from Benjamin and the men of Abner three hundred sixty men who died.

verses.rationale: Keeps paternal tomb, place and overnight return.
verses.before: They lifted up Asahel and buried him in his father’s tomb, which was in Bethlehem. Joab and his men walked all night, and the day dawned upon them at Hebron.
verses.after: They carried Asahel away and buried him in his father’s tomb at Bethlehem. Joab and his men walked all night and reached Hebron at dawn.
verses.tsw_comparator: They lifted up Asahel and buried him in his father’s tomb, which was in Bethlehem. Joab and his men walked all night, and the day dawned upon them at Hebron.

verses.rationale: Retains the paired houses and repeated progressive verbs as a sustained contrast, without reducing house to an individual king.
verses.before: The war between the house of Saul and the house of David was long. David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.
verses.after: The war between Saul’s house and David’s house dragged on. David grew stronger and stronger, while Saul’s house grew weaker and weaker.
verses.tsw_comparator: The war between the house of Saul and the house of David was long. David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.

verses.rationale: Follows the read form for were born and explicitly identifies the maternal relationship.
verses.before: Sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite;
verses.after: Sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, whose mother was Ahinoam of Jezreel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite;

verses.rationale: Preserves Chileab rather than substituting the name in another genealogy; clarifies the two maternal relationships and royal ancestry.
verses.before: his second was Chileab, by Abigail, wife of Nabal the Carmelite; the third was Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
verses.after: His second was Chileab, whose mother was Abigail, Nabal’s widow from Carmel. The third was Absalom, the son of Maacah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur.
verses.tsw_comparator: his second was Chileab, by Abigail, wife of Nabal the Carmelite; the third was Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;

verses.rationale: Keeps the ordinal sequence and each mother attached to her son.
verses.before: the fourth was Adonijah son of Haggith; the fifth was Shephatiah son of Abital;
verses.after: The fourth was Adonijah, the son of Haggith, and the fifth was Shephatiah, the son of Abital.
verses.tsw_comparator: the fourth was Adonijah son of Haggith; the fifth was Shephatiah son of Abital;

verses.rationale: Retains the particular designation wife of David for Eglah and the closing Hebron repetition.
verses.before: and the sixth was Ithream, by Eglah, David’s wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
verses.after: The sixth was Ithream, whose mother was David’s wife Eglah. These sons were born to David in Hebron.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the sixth was Ithream, by Eglah, David’s wife. These were born to David in Hebron.

verses.rationale: Takes the reflexive verb as Abner consolidating his position, while preserving the house language of verse 1.
verses.before: While there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner was making himself strong in the house of Saul.
verses.after: During the war between Saul’s house and David’s house, Abner was strengthening his position in Saul’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: While there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner was making himself strong in the house of Saul.

verses.rationale: Supplies Ish-bosheth from verse 8 for the unnamed speaker; renders the sexual idiom directly while leaving the allegation in his speech.
verses.before: Saul had a concubine whose name was Rizpah daughter of Aiah. Ish-Bosheth said to Abner, “Why did you go in to my father’s concubine?”
verses.after: Saul had had a concubine named Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. Ish-bosheth said to Abner, “Why have you slept with my father’s concubine?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul had a concubine whose name was Rizpah daughter of Aiah. Ish-Bosheth said to Abner, “Why did you go in to my father’s concubine?”

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult Judah phrase and dog-head insult; treats steadfast love as Abner’s claim and does not invent either a confession or a denial.
verses.before: Then Abner became very angry over the words of Ish-Bosheth and said, “Am I a dog’s head that belongs to Judah? This day I show steadfast love to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers, and to his companions, and I have not given you into the hand of David, yet today you charge me with guilt concerning this woman!
verses.after: Abner was furious at Ish-bosheth’s words. “Am I a dog’s head that belongs to Judah?” he said. “To this day I have shown steadfast love to the house of your father Saul, to his brothers, and to his friends. I have not handed you over to David. Yet today you charge me with wrongdoing over this woman!
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Abner became very angry over the words of Ish-Bosheth and said, “Am I a dog’s head that belongs to Judah? This day I show steadfast love to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers, and to his companions, and I have not given you into the hand of David, yet today you charge me with guilt concerning this woman!

verses.rationale: Preserves the third-person self-curse and its unnamed penalty; unfolds the oath condition into natural English.
verses.before: Thus may God do to Abner and more also, if I do not do for David just as the LORD swore to him:
verses.after: May God do this to Abner, and more besides, if I do not carry out for David what the LORD swore to him:
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus may God do to Abner and more also, if I do not do for David just as the LORD swore to him:

verses.rationale: Keeps both political names, the transfer of the kingdom, and the geographical endpoints.
verses.before: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and establish the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beersheba.”
verses.after: to transfer the kingdom from Saul’s house and establish David’s throne over Israel and Judah, from Dan to Beersheba.”
verses.tsw_comparator: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and establish the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beersheba.”

verses.rationale: Makes the frightened speaker identifiable without changing the cause of his silence.
verses.before: Ish-Bosheth could not answer Abner another word because he feared him.
verses.after: Ish-bosheth could not say another word to Abner, because he was afraid of him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ish-Bosheth could not answer Abner another word because he feared him.

verses.rationale: Takes the difficult location or representation expression as on his behalf; retains the open rhetorical question and hand image rather than supplying its answer.
verses.before: Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, “Whose is the land?” and saying, “Make your covenant with me, and look, my hand will be with you to bring all Israel over to you.”
verses.after: Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, “Whose land is it? Make your covenant with me. My hand will be with you to bring all Israel over to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, “Whose is the land?” and saying, “Make your covenant with me, and look, my hand will be with you to bring all Israel over to you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the face repetition and the condition concerning Michal without adding her consent or a romantic motive.
verses.before: David said, “Good. I will make a covenant with you. Only one thing I ask from you: you will not see my face unless you first bring Michal daughter of Saul when you come to see my face.”
verses.after: “Good,” David replied. “I will make a covenant with you. But I require one thing: you will not see my face unless you bring Michal, Saul’s daughter, when you come to see me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said, “Good. I will make a covenant with you. Only one thing I ask from you: you shall not see my face unless you first bring Michal daughter of Saul when you come to see my face.”

verses.rationale: Keeps David’s marital claim and the bodily bride-price; retains a hundred here despite the two hundred delivered in 1 Samuel 18.
verses.before: David sent messengers to Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, saying, “Give me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for one hundred foreskins of the Philistines.”
verses.after: David also sent messengers to Ish-bosheth son of Saul: “Give me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred Philistine foreskins.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David sent messengers to Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, saying, “Give me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for one hundred foreskins of the Philistines.”

verses.rationale: Retains the narrator’s designation husband and the forcible transfer, following the read form Laish.
verses.before: So Ish-Bosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Paltiel son of Laish.
verses.after: So Ish-bosheth had her taken from her husband, Paltiel son of Laish.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Ish-Bosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Paltiel son of Laish.

verses.rationale: Preserves the husband’s sustained grief and Abner’s abrupt order; does not supply Michal’s unreported response.
verses.before: Her husband went with her, walking and weeping behind her as far as Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, “Go, return.” And he returned.
verses.after: Her husband followed her, weeping as he walked, all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner told him, “Go back!” And he went back.
verses.tsw_comparator: Her husband went with her, walking and weeping behind her as far as Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, “Go, return.” And he returned.

verses.rationale: Renders the yesterday and third-day idiom as sustained prior desire while preserving the elders’ agency.
verses.before: Abner had spoken with the elders of Israel, saying, “For some time past you have been seeking David as king over you.
verses.after: Abner had been speaking with the elders of Israel: “For some time now you have wanted David to be your king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abner had spoken with the elders of Israel, saying, “For some time past you have been seeking David as king over you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the paired hands and my servant and my people language; the divine promise remains within Abner’s appeal.
verses.before: Now do it, for the LORD has spoken concerning David, saying, ‘By the hand of David my servant I will save my people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from the hand of all their enemies.’”
verses.after: Now act on it! For the LORD said of David, ‘By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from all their enemies.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now do it, for the LORD has spoken concerning David, saying, ‘By the hand of David my servant I will save my people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from the hand of all their enemies.’”

verses.rationale: Unfolds speaking in the ears and good in the eyes as direct consultation and agreement, retaining Benjamin’s separate involvement.
verses.before: Abner also spoke in the ears of Benjamin. Then Abner went to speak in the ears of David at Hebron all that was good in the eyes of Israel and in the eyes of all the house of Benjamin.
verses.after: Abner also spoke directly with the Benjaminites. Then he went to Hebron to tell David everything that Israel and the whole house of Benjamin had agreed on.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abner also spoke in the ears of Benjamin. Then Abner went to speak in the ears of David at Hebron all that was good in the eyes of Israel and in the eyes of all the house of Benjamin.

verses.rationale: Preserves twenty companions and David’s hospitality without adding a treaty ceremony.
verses.before: Abner came to David at Hebron, and twenty men were with him. David made a feast for Abner and the men who were with him.
verses.after: When Abner came to David at Hebron with twenty men, David made a feast for him and the men with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abner came to David at Hebron, and twenty men were with him. David made a feast for Abner and the men who were with him.

verses.rationale: Retains the covenant proposal and scope of David’s desire; begins the repeated went in peace motif.
verses.before: Abner said to David, “I will arise and go and gather all Israel to my lord the king, so that they may make a covenant with you, and you may reign over all that your life desires.” Then David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.
verses.after: Abner said to David, “Let me go and gather all Israel to my lord the king. They will make a covenant with you, and you will rule over all your heart desires.” David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abner said to David, “I will arise and go and gather all Israel to my lord the king, so that they may make a covenant with you, and you may reign over all that your life desires.” Then David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.

verses.rationale: Retains the plunder and repeats the peaceful departure as the narrator does.
verses.before: And look, the servants of David and Joab came from a raid and brought with them much plunder. But Abner was not with David in Hebron, for David had sent him away and he had gone in peace.
verses.after: Just then David’s men and Joab came back from a raid, bringing a great deal of plunder. Abner was no longer with David in Hebron, for David had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: And look, the servants of David and Joab came from a raid and brought with them much plunder. But Abner was not with David in Hebron, for David had sent him away and he had gone in peace.

verses.rationale: Preserves the third account of the peaceful departure, now as news to Joab.
verses.before: When Joab and all the army that was with him came, they told Joab, saying, “Abner son of Ner came to the king, and he sent him away, and he went in peace.”
verses.after: When Joab and the whole force with him arrived, he was told, “Abner son of Ner came to the king, and the king sent him away. He went in peace.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When Joab and all the army that was with him came, they told Joab, saying, “Abner son of Ner came to the king, and he sent him away, and he went in peace.”

verses.rationale: Maintains the accusation and emphatic departure rather than converting them to a polite question.
verses.before: Then Joab went to the king and said, “What have you done? Look, Abner came to you. Why did you send him away, and he has gone, gone away?
verses.after: Joab went to the king and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you! Why did you send him away and let him go?
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Joab went to the king and said, “What have you done? Look, Abner came to you. Why did you send him away, and he has gone, gone away?

verses.rationale: Keeps Joab’s espionage allegation as speech and follows the read plural for comings.
verses.before: You know Abner son of Ner, that he came to deceive you and to know your going out and your coming in and to know all that you are doing.”
verses.after: You know Abner son of Ner! He came to deceive you, to learn your comings and goings and find out everything you are doing.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You know Abner son of Ner, that he came to deceive you and to know your going out and your coming in and to know all that you are doing.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the cistern location and the narrator’s explicit exclusion of David’s knowledge.
verses.before: Joab went out from David and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the cistern of Sirah, but David did not know it.
verses.after: After leaving David, Joab sent messengers after Abner. They brought him back from the cistern of Sirah, but David knew nothing about it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joab went out from David and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the cistern of Sirah, but David did not know it.

verses.rationale: Makes the deceptive approach readable while noting the uncertain privately or quietly expression; preserves the belly wound and blood vengeance motive.
verses.before: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the middle of the gate to speak with him quietly, and there he struck him in the belly so that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.
verses.after: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside inside the gate, as if to speak privately with him. There he stabbed him in the belly, and Abner died—for the blood of Joab’s brother Asahel.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the middle of the gate to speak with him quietly, and there he struck him in the belly so that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.

verses.rationale: Keeps the declaration as David’s claim and preserves its perpetual scope and blood language.
verses.before: Afterward, when David heard of it, he said, “I and my kingdom are innocent before the LORD forever from the blood of Abner son of Ner.
verses.after: When David heard about it afterward, he said, “I and my kingdom are forever innocent before the LORD of the blood of Abner son of Ner.
verses.tsw_comparator: Afterward, when David heard of it, he said, “I and my kingdom are innocent before the LORD forever from the blood of Abner son of Ner.

verses.rationale: Retains all five elements of the curse, including the difficult spindle image; does not replace it silently with a crutch or moralize illness.
verses.before: May it fall upon the head of Joab and upon all his father’s house. May there never fail from the house of Joab one who has a discharge, or skin disease, or one who holds a spindle, or one who falls by the sword, or one who lacks bread.”
verses.after: May it fall on Joab’s head and on his father’s whole house! May Joab’s house never be without someone with a discharge or a defiling skin disease, someone who holds a spindle, someone who falls by the sword, or someone who lacks bread.”
verses.tsw_comparator: May it fall upon the head of Joab and upon all his father’s house. May there never fail from the house of Joab one who has a discharge, or skin disease, or one who holds a spindle, or one who falls by the sword, or one who lacks bread.”

verses.rationale: Retains the narrator’s attribution to both brothers without inventing Abishai’s precise part in the murder.
verses.before: So Joab and Abishai his brother killed Abner because he had put Asahel their brother to death in the battle at Gibeon.
verses.after: Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had put their brother Asahel to death in the battle at Gibeon.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joab and Abishai his brother killed Abner because he had put Asahel their brother to death in the battle at Gibeon.

verses.rationale: Preserves Joab’s inclusion in the commanded mourning and the funeral image of a bier.
verses.before: David said to Joab and to all the people who were with him, “Tear your clothes, gird yourselves with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner.” And King David walked behind the bier.
verses.after: David told Joab and all the people with him, “Tear your clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourn for Abner.” King David walked behind the bier.
verses.tsw_comparator: David said to Joab and to all the people who were with him, “Tear your clothes, gird yourselves with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner.” And King David walked behind the bier.

verses.rationale: Keeps the grave, the king’s audible weeping, and the people’s answering grief.
verses.before: They buried Abner at Hebron, and the king lifted up his voice and wept at Abner’s grave, and all the people wept.
verses.after: They buried Abner in Hebron. The king wept aloud at Abner’s grave, and all the people wept.
verses.tsw_comparator: They buried Abner at Hebron, and the king lifted up his voice and wept at Abner’s grave, and all the people wept.

verses.rationale: Marks the change to lament within the verse paragraph and retains the question about the manner of death.
verses.before: The king lamented for Abner and said: “Should Abner die as a fool dies?
verses.after: The king sang this lament for Abner: “Should Abner die as a fool dies?
verses.tsw_comparator: The king lamented for Abner and said: “Should Abner die as a fool dies?

verses.rationale: Preserves the paired limbs, bronze restraints, and comparison with falling before wrongdoers; separates the concluding narration from the poem by a line break.
verses.before: Your hands were not bound, and your feet were not put into bronze chains. As one falls before sons of wickedness, you fell.” And all the people wept over him again.
verses.after: Your hands were not bound, and your feet were not put in bronze shackles. You fell as one falls before violent men.” And all the people wept for him again.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your hands were not bound, and your feet were not put into bronze chains. As one falls before sons of wickedness, you fell.” And all the people wept over him again.

verses.rationale: Retains the daylight boundary and broad food prohibition in the oath, without specifying the unnamed curse.
verses.before: Then all the people came to cause David to eat bread while it was still day, but David swore, saying, “Thus may God do to me and more also, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun goes down.”
verses.after: While it was still day, all the people came to urge David to eat. But David swore, “May God do this to me, and more besides, if I taste bread or anything else before sunset!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the people came to cause David to eat bread while it was still day, but David swore, saying, “Thus may God do to me and more also, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun goes down.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both the particular approval and the broader repeated assessment rather than treating the repetition as redundant.
verses.before: All the people recognized it, and it was good in their eyes. Everything the king did was good in the eyes of all the people.
verses.after: All the people took notice and approved. Everything the king did pleased all the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the people recognized it, and it was good in their eyes. Everything the king did was good in the eyes of all the people.

verses.rationale: Renders not from the king as absence of royal direction while preserving the narrator’s report of public understanding.
verses.before: So all the people and all Israel knew that day that it had not been from the king to put Abner son of Ner to death.
verses.after: That day all the people and all Israel understood that the king had not ordered the killing of Abner son of Ner.
verses.tsw_comparator: So all the people and all Israel knew that day that it had not been from the king to put Abner son of Ner to death.

verses.rationale: Keeps the rhetorical question, the two descriptions, and fallen as language connecting the lament to the death.
verses.before: The king said to his servants, “Do you not know that a prince and a great man has fallen this day in Israel?
verses.after: The king said to his servants, “Do you not know that a commander, a great man, has fallen in Israel today?
verses.tsw_comparator: The king said to his servants, “Do you not know that a prince and a great man has fallen this day in Israel?

verses.rationale: Preserves the contrast of soft or weak David with hard sons of Zeruiah and leaves the request for divine repayment as David’s speech.
verses.before: I am weak today, though anointed king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too severe for me. May the LORD repay the evildoer according to his evil.”
verses.after: Today I am weak, though anointed king. These men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too hard for me. May the LORD repay the evildoer for his evil.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And I am weak today, though anointed king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too severe for me. May the LORD repay the evildoer according to his evil.”

verses.rationale: Retains the narrator’s relational designation Saul’s son and the bodily image of lost resolve.
verses.before: When Saul’s son heard that Abner had died in Hebron, his hands grew weak, and all Israel was alarmed.
verses.after: When Saul’s son heard that Abner had died in Hebron, his hands fell limp, and all Israel was alarmed.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Saul’s son heard that Abner had died in Hebron, his hands grew weak, and all Israel was alarmed.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the two commanders and their father while keeping the explanatory tribal assignment.
verses.before: Saul’s son had two men who were captains of raiding bands. The name of one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, from the children of Benjamin, for Beeroth also was regarded as belonging to Benjamin.
verses.after: Saul’s son had two men who commanded raiding bands. One was named Baanah and the other Rechab. They were sons of Rimmon of Beeroth, from the tribe of Benjamin, for Beeroth was counted as part of Benjamin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul’s son had two men who were captains of raiding bands. The name of one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, from the children of Benjamin, for Beeroth also was regarded as belonging to Benjamin.

verses.rationale: Preserves the displacement, resident status, and narrator’s continuing time perspective.
verses.before: The Beerothites fled to Gittaim and have lived there as resident aliens to this day.
verses.after: The people of Beeroth had fled to Gittaim and have lived there as resident foreigners to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Beerothites fled to Gittaim and have lived there as resident aliens to this day.

verses.rationale: Keeps the interruption about the surviving son, his age, and the accident without blaming the nurse or replacing physical disability with a metaphor.
verses.before: Jonathan son of Saul had a son crippled in his feet. He was five years old when the report concerning Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse carried him and fled, and as she hurried to flee he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.
verses.after: Jonathan son of Saul had a son whose feet were disabled. He was five years old when news of Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled, but in her hurry to escape he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jonathan son of Saul had a son crippled in his feet. He was five years old when the report concerning Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse carried him and fled, and as she hurried to flee he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.

verses.rationale: Retains the named agents, time of day, and vulnerable resting victim.
verses.before: The sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went and came during the heat of the day to the house of Ish-Bosheth while he was lying down for his midday rest.
verses.after: Rechab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon of Beeroth, set out and reached Ish-bosheth’s house in the heat of the day. He was lying down for his midday rest.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went and came during the heat of the day to the house of Ish-Bosheth while he was lying down for his midday rest.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned Hebrew wheat-taking account; as though marks the inferred pretext rather than importing a different doorway scene.
verses.before: They came there into the midst of the house as if to get wheat, and they struck him in the belly. Then Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.
verses.after: They entered the inner part of the house as though to get wheat and stabbed him in the belly. Then Rechab and his brother Baanah escaped.
verses.tsw_comparator: They came there into the midst of the house as though to get wheat, and they struck him in the belly. Then Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated account of entering and killing, all three violent actions, and the head carried through the night.
verses.before: They entered the house while he was lying on his bed in his bedroom, struck him and put him to death, and cut off his head. They took his head and walked by the way of the Arabah all night.
verses.after: They had entered the house while he was lying on his bed in his bedroom. They struck him, killed him, and cut off his head. Taking his head, they traveled through the Arabah all night.
verses.tsw_comparator: They entered the house while he was lying on his bed in his bedroom, struck him and put him to death, and cut off his head. They took his head and walked by the way of the Arabah all night.

verses.rationale: Retains the murderers’ claim of divine vengeance as their interpretation, not narrator endorsement, and preserves offspring.
verses.before: They brought the head of Ish-Bosheth to David at Hebron and said to the king, “Look, the head of Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, your enemy who sought your life. The LORD has given my lord the king vengeance this day upon Saul and upon his offspring.”
verses.after: They brought Ish-bosheth’s head to David at Hebron and said to the king, “Here is the head of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, your enemy who sought your life. Today the LORD has given my lord the king vengeance on Saul and his offspring.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They brought the head of Ish-Bosheth to David at Hebron and said to the king, “Look, the head of Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, your enemy who sought your life. The LORD has given my lord the king vengeance this day upon Saul and upon his offspring.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the living-LORD oath and redeemed language rather than reducing it to a generic declaration.
verses.before: David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, “As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from every distress,
verses.after: David answered Rechab and his brother Baanah, the sons of Rimmon of Beeroth: “As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from every distress,
verses.tsw_comparator: David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, “As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from every distress,

verses.rationale: Makes the ironic reward clause intelligible while preserving David’s own compressed account of the earlier execution.
verses.before: when one told me, saying, ‘Look, Saul is dead,’ and he was in his own eyes like one bringing good news, I seized him and killed him at Ziklag. That was the reward I gave him for his good news.
verses.after: when someone told me, ‘Saul is dead,’ thinking he brought good news, I seized him and killed him at Ziklag. That was my reward for his news!
verses.tsw_comparator: when one told me, saying, ‘Look, Saul is dead,’ and he was in his own eyes like one bringing good news, I seized him and killed him at Ziklag. That was the reward I gave him for his good news.

verses.rationale: Keeps David’s moral contrast, the victim’s location, and the demand for blood from the killers’ hands.
verses.before: How much more when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his own house on his bed! And now, will I not seek his blood from your hand and remove you from the earth?”
verses.after: How much more, then, when wicked men have killed an innocent man in his own house, on his bed! Should I not demand his blood from your hands and remove you from the earth?”
verses.tsw_comparator: How much more when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his own house on his bed! And now, shall I not seek his blood from your hand and remove you from the earth?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the execution, mutilation, public display, and contrasting burial without sanitizing David’s punishment.
verses.before: Then David commanded the young men, and they killed them and cut off their hands and feet and hung them beside the pool at Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-Bosheth and buried it in the grave of Abner at Hebron.
verses.after: David gave orders to his young men, and they killed the brothers. They cut off their hands and feet and hung them beside the pool in Hebron. But they took Ish-bosheth’s head and buried it in Abner’s tomb at Hebron.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then David commanded the young men, and they killed them and cut off their hands and feet and hung them beside the pool at Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-Bosheth and buried it in the grave of Abner at Hebron.

verses.rationale: Retains the kinship image instead of replacing it with a political abstraction.
verses.before: Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, “Look, we are your bone and your flesh.
verses.after: All the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, “We are your own bone and flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, “Look, we are your bone and your flesh.

verses.rationale: Follows the read forms for past leadership and preserves the shepherd image and distinction between ruler and king.
verses.before: Even formerly, when Saul was king over us, you were the one leading Israel out and bringing Israel in. And the LORD said to you, ‘You will shepherd my people Israel, and you will be ruler over Israel.’”
verses.after: Even when Saul was king over us, you were the one who led Israel out and brought Israel back. And the LORD said to you, ‘You will shepherd my people Israel; you will be ruler over Israel.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Even formerly, when Saul was king over us, you were the one leading Israel out and bringing Israel in. And the LORD said to you, ‘You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be ruler over Israel.’”

verses.rationale: Retains elders as agents, covenant before the LORD, and the wider anointing distinct from Judah’s in chapter 2.
verses.before: So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD. Then they anointed David king over Israel.
verses.after: All the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron. King David made a covenant with them there before the LORD, and they anointed David king over Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD. Then they anointed David king over Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves the stated age and overall reign without correcting the rounded total using the following verse.
verses.before: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.
verses.after: David was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years.
verses.tsw_comparator: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

verses.rationale: Keeps both durations and their respective political and geographical scopes.
verses.before: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.
verses.after: He reigned over Judah in Hebron for seven years and six months. In Jerusalem he reigned over all Israel and Judah for thirty-three years.
verses.tsw_comparator: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.

verses.rationale: Takes the difficult exclusion clause as the defenders’ taunt; preserves its disability language as their speech and flags the alternative unless you remove reading.
verses.before: The king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land. They said to David, “You will not come in here; even the blind and the lame will turn you away,” thinking, “David cannot come in here.”
verses.after: The king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites who lived in the land. They told David, “You will not get in here! Even the blind and the lame will turn you back.” They thought, “David will never get in here.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land. They said to David, “You will not come in here; even the blind and the lame will turn you away,” thinking, “David cannot come in here.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the surprise reversal and the identification of Zion with the City of David.
verses.before: Yet David captured the stronghold of Zion; that is, the city of David.
verses.after: But David captured the stronghold of Zion, which is the City of David.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet David captured the stronghold of Zion; that is, the city of David.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult water-shaft clause, the read form hated by David, and the exclusionary saying; does not complete the sentence with a reward borrowed from another account or identify the house as the temple.
verses.before: David said on that day, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites, let him reach the water shaft, and the lame and the blind, whom David’s life hates.” Therefore they say, “The blind and the lame will not come into the house.”
verses.after: That day David said, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites must reach the water shaft—and the lame and the blind, those David hates.” That is why people say, “The blind and the lame must not enter the house.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David said on that day, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites, let him reach the water shaft, and the lame and the blind, whom David’s life hates.” Therefore they say, “The blind and the lame shall not come into the house.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the named Millo and inward direction rather than inventing a precise architectural reconstruction.
verses.before: David lived in the stronghold and called it the city of David. David built around it from the Millo inward.
verses.after: David settled in the stronghold and called it the City of David. He built up the surrounding area, from the Millo inward.
verses.tsw_comparator: David lived in the stronghold and called it the city of David. David built around it from the Millo inward.

verses.rationale: Retains the progressive repetition and the full divine title, linking power with the presence statement.
verses.before: David grew greater and greater, and the LORD, the God of Hosts, was with him.
verses.after: David grew greater and greater, and the LORD, the God of Armies, was with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: David grew greater and greater, and the LORD, the God of Hosts, was with him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the ruler, materials, and two kinds of craftsmen; retains house rather than making the palace interpretation obligatory.
verses.before: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, with cedar trees, carpenters, and stonemasons, and they built a house for David.
verses.after: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar timber, carpenters, and stonemasons. They built a house for David.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, with cedar trees, carpenters, and stonemasons, and they built a house for David.

verses.rationale: Preserves the stated beneficiary of the kingdom, the people, and David’s recognition as the perspective.
verses.before: David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had exalted his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.
verses.after: David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had raised up his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had exalted his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains both relationship categories and daughters as well as sons, without adding praise for the expanding household.
verses.before: David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem after he came from Hebron, and more sons and daughters were born to David.
verses.after: After coming from Hebron, David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters were born to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem after he came from Hebron, and more sons and daughters were born to David.

verses.rationale: Keeps the list’s introduction and its first four names, continuing the sentence across verse labels.
verses.before: These are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
verses.after: These are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,

verses.rationale: Preserves all four names and their order without substituting names from parallel genealogies.
verses.before: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
verses.after: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
verses.tsw_comparator: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,

verses.rationale: Completes the eleven-name list with the pinned forms and order.
verses.before: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
verses.after: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.

verses.rationale: Preserves the trigger, search, and opposing directions without identifying the stronghold beyond the text.
verses.before: When the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David. David heard of it and went down to the stronghold.
verses.after: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, all the Philistines came up in search of him. David heard about it and went down to the stronghold.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David. David heard of it and went down to the stronghold.

verses.rationale: Retains the deployment and named valley as the setting for both encounters.
verses.before: The Philistines came and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.after: The Philistines came and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistines came and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.

verses.rationale: Keeps both questions, the repeated hand image, and the emphatic promise.
verses.before: David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Will I go up against the Philistines? Will you give them into my hand?” The LORD said to David, “Go up, for I will surely give the Philistines into your hand.”
verses.after: David asked the LORD, “Should I go up against the Philistines? Will you give them into my hand?” The LORD answered, “Go up. I will certainly give the Philistines into your hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you give them into my hand?” The LORD said to David, “Go up, for I will surely give the Philistines into your hand.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the water image and naming explanation rather than flattening the repeated breakthrough language.
verses.before: David came to Baal-Perazim, and David struck them there. He said, “The LORD has broken through my enemies before me like a breakthrough of waters.” Therefore he called the name of that place Baal-Perazim.
verses.after: David went to Baal-perazim and defeated them there. He said, “The LORD has broken through my enemies before me like a burst of water.” That is why he named the place Baal-perazim.
verses.tsw_comparator: David came to Baal-Perazim, and David struck them there. He said, “The LORD has broken through my enemies before me like a breakthrough of waters.” Therefore he called the name of that place Baal-Perazim.

verses.rationale: Retains carried away; does not import burning from a parallel account.
verses.before: They abandoned their idols there, and David and his men carried them away.
verses.after: The Philistines abandoned their idols there, and David and his men carried them away.
verses.tsw_comparator: They abandoned their idols there, and David and his men carried them away.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated attack and nearly repeated deployment language.
verses.before: The Philistines came up again and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.after: Once again the Philistines came up and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistines came up again and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.

verses.rationale: Makes the changed approach clear while treating balsam as an uncertain tree identification rather than a botanical certainty.
verses.before: David inquired of the LORD, and he said, “You will not go up. Circle around behind them and come against them opposite the balsam trees.
verses.after: David asked the LORD, and he answered, “Do not go straight up. Circle around behind them and approach them opposite the balsam trees.
verses.tsw_comparator: David inquired of the LORD, and he said, “You shall not go up. Circle around behind them and come against them opposite the balsam trees.

verses.rationale: Follows the read when and retains the audible marching above and divine advance, without reducing the sound to ordinary wind.
verses.before: When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then act decisively, for then the LORD has gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”
verses.after: When you hear the sound of marching in the treetops, act decisively. Then the LORD will have gone out ahead of you to strike the Philistine camp.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then act decisively, for then the LORD has gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”

verses.rationale: Retains pinned Geba rather than substituting Gibeon from a parallel account.
verses.before: David did so, as the LORD commanded him, and struck the Philistines from Geba as far as Gezer.
verses.after: David did as the LORD commanded him and struck down the Philistines from Geba all the way to Gezer.
verses.tsw_comparator: David did so, as the LORD commanded him, and struck the Philistines from Geba as far as Gezer.
